newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Greenpeace pipes up against Olympic plastic.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Greenpeace pipes up against Olympic plastic.

text.p: Greenpeace activists staged a dawn raid on Wednesday at the site of the Sydney 2000 Olympics, digging up PVC plastic piping and dumping it at the site office.
The environmental group said Olympic organisers had broken an agreement to minimise their use of PVC (polyvinyl chloride) to reduce possible health and environmental risks.

"Someone is cutting corners here and the reputation of Sydney's Green Games is at stake," said Greenpeace Olympics campaigner Michael Bland, who took part in the protest at the Homebush Bay Olympic site.
PVC manufacturers disagreed, saying Greenpeace's publicity stunt carried "the trademark of an organisation that is out of touch with the scientific facts".
"PVC is inert, insoluble, inedible, non-toxic and an outstanding building material," said the Plastics and Chemicals Industries Association in a statement.
It quoted Sydney chemistry professor Michael Gallagher as saying: "The only way you could harm anyone with it (PVC) would be to hit them over the head".

Bland said the use of PVC piping was in breach of the Sydney Olympic bid document -- supported by Greenpeace -- which says use of PVC and other chlorine-based products should be kept to a minimum or avoided altogether.
He said 25 Greenpeace activists had found several kilometres of PVC piping on the Olympic site at Homebush Bay in western Sydney, even though alternative materials were readily available.
Olympic site environment manager Colin Grant said PVC piping was only being used for electrical and telephone underground cabling as it was a good insulator and resistant to fire.
"There is not an alternative that has the same property at a competitive price -- and price has to be taken into account," Grant told reporters.
